title: Log triage
lede: Most log lines are routine and a rule can say so instantly. A few are not, and no rule you have written yet knows which. Expanso shapes, fingerprints and counts every record, sends known routine lines straight to the archive, and asks Jev only about what is left.

stages.title: Shape and fingerprint
stages.text: Adds received_at, node_id and a fingerprint: the service plus the message with every number replaced by #. Also adds the baseline, what severity-only routing would have done with the same record.

stages.title: Count occurrences
stages.text: Asks the local counter (POST /track) how many times this fingerprint has been seen in the last 10 minutes and what was decided before. The answer is stored under recurrence.

stages.title: Mark the route
stages.text: Records that Expanso, not a model, handled this record.

stages.title: Prepare the log line
stages.text: Builds the operational log summary in message metadata. It carries closed-set values and hashes only, never the message text. The record itself does not change.

stages.title: Write the log line
stages.text: Emits an Expanso Cloud log line on a fingerprint's first occurrence and on every 250th after it. The record itself does not change.

stages.title: Archive
stages.text: Every record is written, now structured and counted, to data/logs.jsonl. No model is in this pipeline.

stages.title: Wait if held
stages.text: A record coming back from a hold waits 2 to 4 seconds, jittered so a recovery is not a stampede. First arrivals pass through untouched.

stages.title: Shape and fingerprint
stages.text: Adds received_at, node_id, the fingerprint, held_attempts (coerced to a whole number at least 0) and the severity-only baseline.

stages.title: Count occurrences
stages.text: First arrival only: asks the counter how many times this fingerprint has been seen in 10 minutes and what was decided before. A held record is the same event, so it is not counted again.

stages.title: Skip the model for routine lines
stages.text: An exact allowlist of level INFO, service and raw message. A match sets bypass and goes to the archive with no model call. Any changed number, any WARN or ERROR and any novel INFO line is judged.

stages.title: Ask Jev
stages.text: For records that were not bypassed: one request with the record, its recurrence history and four questions (actionable, severity, team, recurrence concern). Bypassed records skip this stage. If Jev does not answer, the catch block marks the answer unavailable.

stages.title: Decide
stages.text: Bypass archives. No answer and fewer than 15 attempts holds. No answer after 15 attempts goes to review. Critical at confidence 0.85 or more pages. Actionable 0.7 or more at confidence 0.5 or more notifies. Confidence under 0.6, or actionable from 0.4 to under 0.7, goes to review. Everything else archives.

stages.title: Prepare the log line
stages.text: Builds the operational log summary in message metadata from closed sets and hashes. The record itself does not change.

stages.title: Write the log line
stages.text: Logs every judged or held selection, and a bypass checkpoint on a fingerprint's first occurrence and every 250th. The record itself does not change.

stages.title: Record the decision
stages.text: Sends the decision to the counter (POST /record) so the next occurrence sees it in its history. Not done while a record is held.

stages.title: Route to a bucket
stages.text: A switch writes the record to page, notify, review or archive. A held record writes a receipt to held first, then is posted back to this pipeline's own input to ask again.

outage.note: Jev answers 503. The two routine lines still reach the archive with no model call. The WARN record is held: one receipt is written, then it is posted back to the input every 2 to 4 seconds and handed to review after 15 attempts, about 45 seconds. Nothing is guessed and nothing is dropped.

run.title: Run it with no account
run.intro: The fixture runner deploys each pipeline exactly as shipped to a local Edge agent, starts the recurrence counter the pipelines call, posts every line of `input.jsonl`, and compares what the pipeline wrote with the expected output. A third case makes Jev unreachable and watches a record being held and then handed to review. It needs expanso-edge, expanso-cli and uv.
run.after: Each case prints pass or FAIL with the buckets it wrote.

run.title: Run the live board
run.intro: The board watches a real pipeline in three acts: nothing deployed, Expanso alone, Expanso and Jev. It needs Expanso Cloud credentials and either a TypeSafe key or the bundled responder.
commands:
just init
just jev-key
just doctor

just up triage
just open triage
run.after: `demos/01-log-triage/README.md` explains the board and what to do when it breaks.

deploy.title: Deploy through Expanso Cloud
deploy.intro: Both files deploy as the same job, `log-triage`, so act three is a version bump of act two. Credentials come from the environment, never from flags.
deploy.after: The recurrence pipeline asks `JEV_API_URL`, which defaults to the local responder on 127.0.0.1:8099. Point it at the dashboard server's gate (the live demo does) or at Jev with `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` set in the Edge agent's environment. The counter at 127.0.0.1:8898 is `demos/01-log-triage/counter.py`; replace it with a store you trust before real traffic.
